member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Evaluation.BondConductance
member.summary: Average per-cluster graph conductance on the bond-probability-weighted graph: for each cluster c, φ(c) = cut(c) / min(vol(c), 2m − vol(c)); the evaluator returns the mean of φ(c) across non-trivial clusters.

remarks.para:
Definitions.
cut(c) = Σ_{i ∈ c, j ∉ c} w_ij — bond weight on edges crossing cluster c's boundary.
vol(c) = Σ_{i ∈ c} k_i — weighted degree sum inside c.
2m = Σ_i k_i — total weighted-degree mass.
Each cross-boundary edge contributes its weight to both endpoint clusters' cut counts (it leaves both sides), so the per-cluster cut is accumulated symmetrically.

Range. [0, 1]. Lower is better. A well-isolated cluster has nearly all its bond weight internal — conductance near 0. A cluster that's mostly boundary has conductance approaching 1. Average across clusters gives a partition-level score where small values indicate the cut respects bond density (clusters are tightly bound, weakly leaving).

Why pair with modularity + coverage.
Modularity: null-model-adjusted internal density (global).
Coverage: raw internal fraction (global).
Conductance: per-cluster boundary tightness, averaged.
Together they triangulate "is this a good cut" from three orthogonal angles.

Edge cases. A single cluster has cut 0 and conductance 0 (perfect by this metric — degenerate). Empty / single-node graphs return 0. Clusters whose min(vol(c), 2m − vol(c)) is zero are skipped from the average (the formula is undefined).
Requires. Tier 1 edge observables.

member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Evaluation.BondCoverage
member.summary: Fraction of total bond weight that lies within clusters: Coverage = (Σ_{ij: c_i=c_j} w_ij) / (Σ_{ij} w_ij).

remarks.para: Reading. Raw "internal density" — what fraction of the SW dynamics' bond activity is captured inside the partition's clusters. Range [0, 1]; higher is better. Complements : coverage is the unadjusted internal fraction; modularity is the same quantity adjusted against a degree- preserving null model.

Edge cases. Returns 0 when there are no bonds (total weight zero); returns 1 when the partition has a single cluster (every edge is internal). Singleton clusters drop coverage toward 0 because every edge becomes a cut.

Why pair with modularity. Coverage rewards lumping everything into one cluster; modularity penalizes that. Reading both gives a more honest view than either alone: high coverage + low modularity = "trivial big-cluster partition"; high coverage + high modularity = "genuinely community-shaped."
Requires. Tier 1 edge observables.

member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Evaluation.BondModularity
member.summary: Newman-Girvan modularity on the bond-probability-weighted graph. Quantifies how much more strongly nodes are bonded within their assigned cluster than would be expected from a random graph with the same weighted degree sequence.

remarks.para: Definition. Q = (1/2m) Σ_{ij} [w_ij − k_i·k_j / 2m] · δ(c_i, c_j) where w_ij = ⟨ω(e)⟩ is the equilibrium bond probability, k_i = Σ_j w_ij is the weighted degree, m = (1/2) Σ_i k_i is the total edge weight, and δ(c_i, c_j) = 1 when both nodes share a cluster.

Range. [-0.5, 1]. Positive = the partition captures more within-cluster bond weight than the null model expects; values near 0 = random-quality; strongly negative = the partition cuts where bonds are densest. Higher is better.
Edge cases. Returns 0 for trivial cases (no edges, no nodes, zero total weight). Single-cluster partition trivially scores 0. Singleton clusters score negatively.
Requires. Tier 1 edge observables.

member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Observables.Projections.BondFrequencyBinaryEntropySum
member.summary: Per-node sum of binary entropies of incident bond probabilities: V_i = Σ_{j ∈ N(i)} H_2(⟨ω(i,j)⟩) where H_2(p) = −p log₂ p − (1−p) log₂(1−p).

remarks.para: Interpretation. Binary entropy is zero when the bond frequency saturates at 0 or 1 (the edge is permanently broken or permanently fused — empty space or deep core respectively) and peaks at p = 0.5 (the edge is "flickering" — forming on roughly half of SW cycles). Summed over a node's incident edges, V_i is high for nodes whose neighborhoods sit on volatile boundaries — the structural fracture lines of the dataset.

Subject / Op decomposition. Subject: BondFrequency (per-edge ⟨ω(e)⟩). Op: BinaryEntropySum — a composite operation reading as "pointwise binary entropy on each edge, summed over node's incident edges to produce a per-node scalar."
Units. Result is in bits. The natural-log binary entropy −(p ln p + (1−p) ln(1−p)) is computed internally for numerical stability, then divided by ln 2.
CSR-walk convention. Same upper-triangular pattern as ; each edge's binary entropy is accumulated into both endpoints.
Requires. Tier 1 edge observables.

member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Observables.Projections.IGraphSignal
member.summary: A per-node scalar field derived from an SPC run's equilibrium observables. Mathematically a graph signal f: V → ℝ on the proximity graph's vertex set. Each implementation names a distinct measurement; many are routinely composed in a single analysis.

remarks.para: Pattern role. Unlike (alternatives — pick one per analysis), graph signals are distinct measurements — `BondFrequencyDegree` and `BondFrequencyBinaryEntropySum` do not compete; they answer different questions about the same run. The "Strategy" suffix is intentionally omitted — these are not interchangeable approaches to one job.

Naming convention for concrete signals. <Subject><Op> — the family axis is the substrate being measured (BondFrequency, SpinCorrelation, SpinHistogram, SpinSequence, Cluster, ...), the secondary axis is the mathematical operation that reduces that substrate to one scalar per node (Degree, BinaryEntropySum, EigenvectorCentrality, CyclomaticComplexity, Compressibility, ...). This inverts 's <Op><Subject>: partitions vary by how, signals vary by what. The naming order in each family puts the varying axis first.

Op precision. Op tokens name the full mathematical operation, not a category: EigenvectorCentrality not Centrality; CyclomaticComplexity not Cyclomatic; Compressibility (the property measured) rather than a specific estimator (LempelZiv etc.) — estimator choice becomes a configuration parameter, not part of the type identity.

Algebraic closure. Graph signals are closed under pointwise combination (sum, scale, normalize, product). This lets compound signals like "z-score of BondFrequencyDegree" be expressed as combinators over primitive signals; partitions do not compose this way.

Output contract. Returns a double[] of length run.Graph.NodeCount. Implementations that require observable tiers missing from the supplied run throw with a clear message identifying which tier was needed.

member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Observables.Projections.SpinCorrelationEigenvectorCentrality
member.summary: Per-node entry of the top eigenvector of the spin-correlation matrix G_ij = ⟨1_{s_i = s_j}⟩. Reads as eigenvector centrality on the thermodynamic correlation graph: nodes whose entries are large participate strongly in the dominant collective mode of correlated spin fluctuations at equilibrium.

list.item:
Build the dense N×N symmetric matrix G:
G[i,j] = G[j,i] = SpinAgreementCount[e] / CycleCount for every undirected edge (i,j) in the CSR.
G[i,i] = 1 (a node trivially agrees with itself — the correlation matrix convention).
Off-graph pairs default to 0 (no observation; FK-zero baseline). Pairs whose mutual correlation is significant but whose edge was absent from the proximity graph cannot be recovered from this signal.
Call ; the result's eigenvalues are sorted descending.
Take Eigenvectors[0] as the per-node scalar.

By Perron-Frobenius (G is non-negative symmetric) the top eigenvector is sign-uniform. If the solver returned the negative branch, flip the sign so all entries are non-negative — gives callers a canonical, interpretable centrality.

remarks.para: Subject / Op decomposition. Subject: SpinCorrelation (per-pair G_ij = ⟨1_{s_i=s_j}⟩). Op: EigenvectorCentrality (top eigenvector of the symmetric non-negative matrix). The Op name commits to eigenvector centrality specifically — not betweenness, not Katz, not PageRank — and not merely the abstract category Centrality.

Cost. Dense O(N²) memory and O(N³) compute for the eigendecomposition. Suited to typical patch sizes (N ≲ a few hundred); for global SPC on large graphs a Lanczos-style sparse iteration on the symmetric correlation operator would scale better but is not in the current LinAlg surface — revisit if profiling shows this hot.
Requires. Tier 1 edge observables — must be non-null with a populated .

member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Partitions.Hierarchical.BlattPartitionStrategy
member.summary: Hierarchical SPC partitioner in the Blatt 1996 / Blatt-Wiseman-Domany 1997 picture: detect pseudo-transitions on the χ_m trajectory, treat the intervals between consecutive peaks as stable super-paramagnetic phases, run a fresh Tier-1 equilibrium at each phase's representative temperature, and apply the friends-of-friends cut to read off the per-phase partition. The ordered sequence of partitions is the hierarchy.

remarks.para: Inputs. A from any sweep strategy — typically with a dense user-supplied grid that brackets the expected transition range. The strategy ignores sweep.FinalRun entirely; it cares only about sweep.Summary.Profile (for peak detection) and re-samples the equilibrium at each phase representative on its own terms.

Phase representative T. v1 uses the geometric midpoint of each interval between consecutive peaks, with the cold extremum = min(sweep.Temperatures) below the first peak and the hot extremum = max(sweep.Temperatures) above the last peak. The geometric mean is the natural choice on log-spaced T grids and the arithmetic mean degenerates to it on linear grids that don't span a decade. Future variants may pick the local χ_m minimum inside each interval (sharper but noisier).

Nesting check. The Blatt picture predicts strict nesting between consecutive levels — every cluster at a hotter level is a subset of some cluster at the colder level. The strategy validates this against the actual per-phase partitions and reports the verdict in ; the boolean is informational, not a failure (an undersampled or noisy sweep may produce non-nesting levels that are still useful as individual partitions).

member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Partitions.Hierarchical.IPseudoTransitionDetector
member.summary: Detects pseudo-transitions in an SPC sweep — the temperature points where the system reorganizes between super-paramagnetic phases in the Blatt 1996 / Blatt-Wiseman-Domany 1997 picture.

remarks.para: Classical signal. The canonical Blatt detector watches the magnetization susceptibility χ_m = N · (⟨m²⟩ − ⟨m⟩²) / T for peaks. Each peak marks a phase boundary where a cluster of size K_i breaks into K_{i+1} > K_i sub-clusters; between consecutive peaks the system is in a stable super-paramagnetic phase and the canonical friends-of-friends cut yields a clean partition. The default implementation () consumes 's "MagnetizationVariance" channel — N/T scaling is a strict monotone transform and does not change peak locations on a fixed graph, so the raw variance suffices for relative peak detection.

Pluggable. Concrete detectors may swap the signal (specific heat Cv for energy-axis transitions, label entropy for partition-shape jumps) or the discrimination policy (prominence threshold, peak persistence, multi-signal consensus). All return the same shape: a sorted set of temperatures at which a pseudo-transition was detected.

member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Partitions.Hierarchical.MagnetizationPeakDetector
member.summary: Default : scans the magnetization-variance trajectory for local maxima with prominence above . The classical Blatt χ_m peak detector, modulo the N/T pre-scaling that doesn't affect peak location on a fixed graph.

remarks.para: Signal source. Reads 's entry; throws if the channel is absent. populates "MagnetizationVariance" by default, so any sweep run through the standard pipeline is consumable as-is.

Peak rule. A local maximum is recorded when both neighbors are strictly lower AND the maximum's prominence (height above the higher of the two surrounding minima within the window) is at least relative to the signal's peak-to-trough range. Endpoints are never peaks. Repeated equal samples are treated as plateaus and skipped — a plateau is only a peak when it has strict descents on both sides.

Limitations. v1 is a simple three-point scan with a prominence gate; no smoothing, no Savitzky-Golay, no persistence homology. Adequate for sweeps with reasonable sample density and well-separated phases; noisy or undersampled sweeps will need a successor detector (smoothed-spline peak, multi-signal consensus, or BARS-derived posterior modes).

remarks.para: Ordering. is sorted ascending in . The cold-end level is Levels[0]; the hot-end level is Levels[^1]. Consumers that want to walk merges (cold→hot) should iterate ascending; consumers that want to walk splits (hot→cold) iterate descending.

Nesting. The Blatt picture predicts strict nesting: every cluster at a hotter level is a subset of some cluster at a colder level. records whether that invariant actually held for this run; an undersampled or noisy sweep may produce non-nesting levels that are still individually useful as per-phase partitions, just not stackable as a single merge tree.

Not a Clustering.Dendrograms.Dendrogram. Both shapes are hierarchical trees of clusters with a scalar cost axis, but the semantics differ at the foundation. A Clustering.Dendrograms.Dendrogram records pairwise single-linkage merges between subtrees of data points; its cost axis is a dissimilarity (mutual-reachability distance, ΔH, …) that is intrinsic to the geometry of the data. A records phase-resolved partitions along an SPC temperature sweep; its cost axis is the thermodynamic control parameter and each level is the equilibrium clustering at that T, not a pairwise merge event. Don't convert one into the other — the shared "tree of clusters with a y-axis" is a napkin- sketch coincidence, not a structural identity.

member.summary: Single-temperature Swendsen-Wang sampler for the q-state Potts model. Generic over an struct so the JIT can specialize the hot path and dead-code-eliminate the disabled accumulator branch.

remarks.para: Hot-path discipline. No per-cycle allocation. All scratch arrays are fields, sized at construction. Bond probabilities are precomputed once; the inner loop is a table lookup. The bond-formation and energy accumulation share a single edge walk because both decisions key off the same spin-equality test. The j <= i skip handles symmetric CSR (each undirected edge stored as both (i,j) and (j,i)). The FK accumulator widens to on multiply to survive large N.

Color semantics. _spins[i] is a Potts color in [0, q), not a cluster ID. Bond formation reads the OLD spins (Pass 1) and the energy is evaluated against that same configuration. The cluster flip (Pass 2) overwrites _spins with NEW colors, one per UF root. Two distinct bond clusters may independently draw the same color; this is the "color collision" that distinguishes Blatt (which counts color buckets) from FK (which counts UF root sizes directly).

Always-on accumulators. FK χ, specific-heat moments, Blatt magnetization, and the cluster-size histogram are all populated every cycle regardless of . They are free byproducts of the SW union-find pass — gating them would double the specialization count to save a handful of float ops per cycle, which is the wrong trade. Only earns a JIT-specialization gate (it owns the only per-bond scatter write).

member.name: T:Clustering.Graphical.SPC.Runtime.Scheduling.AdaptiveSweepStrategy
member.summary: Three-stage adaptive sweep strategy: coarse log-spaced probe → dense band refinement with multi-replica averaging → final equilibrium at the chosen T. The default implementation and the historical pipeline that the rest of the SPC stack was built against.

remarks.para: Stage 1 — Coarse probe. Log-spaced grid over [TempMin, TempMax]; measures χ_FK at each grid point with a short burn-in + accumulation. Goal: locate the susceptibility peak region.

Stage 2 — Dense refinement with replicas. Identify the half-maximum band around the coarse peak; build a log-spaced grid within that band; for each grid point, run DenseReplicas × DenseRounds independent measurements and average. The (T, replica, round) cartesian product is flattened to a single task list dispatched against the worker budget.

Stage 3 — Final equilibrium. Construct a PottsModel at the chosen T with (defaults to ), run the full burn + accumulate cycle, and return the per-edge observables when the tier provides them. The cut policy consumes these to produce cluster labels.

Early-stop. If the coarse profile already has stability ≥ , skip Stage 2 and go directly to Stage 3 at the coarse peak. Reduces compute when the susceptibility curve is already sharp from the coarse sweep alone.
Susceptibility estimator. χ_FK = ⟨Σ|c|²⟩ / (cycles · N) read directly from PottsModel's running accumulators.
